```{python}
#| output: false
import numpy as np
import polars as pl
import requests
import xgboost as xgb
from pathlib import Path
from plotnine import (
    ggplot, aes, geom_point, geom_line, geom_col, geom_abline, geom_jitter,
    geom_histogram, labs, theme_minimal, coord_flip, facet_wrap,
)
from great_tables import GT
from IPython.display import HTML, display

ROOT = Path.cwd()
while not (ROOT / "python" / "artifacts").is_dir():
    ROOT = ROOT.parent
ART = ROOT / "python" / "artifacts"
CACHE = ROOT / "docs" / "models" / ".cache"
CACHE.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
DL = "https://github.com/sportsdataverse/sportsdataverse-data/releases/download"
def cached(tag, name):
    p = CACHE / name
    if not p.exists():
        r = requests.get(f"{DL}/{tag}/{name}", timeout=900)
        r.raise_for_status()
        p.write_bytes(r.content)
    return pl.read_parquet(p)

# The scored 2025 frame: prefer the stage-10 build-tree output (the same producer as the
# release, and it carries the athlete ids added 2026-09-01); fall back to the release.
_mp_local = ART / "model_pbp_2025.parquet"
if _mp_local.is_file():
    mp = pl.read_parquet(_mp_local)
    mp_source = (f"python/artifacts/model_pbp_2025.parquet (stage 10 build tree, scored {mp['scored_date'][0]} "
                 f"with {mp['cp_model_version'][0]})")
else:
    mp, mp_source = cached("espn_cfb_model_pbp", "model_pbp_2025.parquet"), "espn_cfb_model_pbp release"
ratings = cached("cfb_ratings", "cfb_ratings_2025.parquet")

def gt_show(g):
    display(HTML(g.as_raw_html()))
```

The per-model cards in this directory are **generated** by
`cfb_model_reports` (stage `cfb_model_70_reports`) from the training
pipeline's real artifacts — they are already compiled documents, rebuilt on
every reports run, with LOSO metrics and calibration figures produced by the
same code that trains the models. This page is their **Quarto companion**: a
suite-level deep dive the generator does not own, recomputing the
leave-one-season-out evaluations from the committed out-of-fold artifacts,
attributing the boosters with TreeSHAP, and putting identified, human-readable
results tables on the published surfaces. Everything here is computed at
render time — from `python/artifacts/` (the model pipeline's output tree;
regenerate with `scripts/cfb_models.sh`) and the published releases.

## The corpus

```{python}
pf = pl.scan_parquet(ART / "pbp_full.parquet")
by_season = (
    pf.group_by("season")
    .agg(pl.len().alias("plays"), pl.col("game_id").n_unique().alias("games"),
         pl.col("EPA").mean().alias("mean_epa"))
    .sort("season").collect()
)
gt_show(
    GT(by_season.tail(10).to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Training corpus (python/artifacts/pbp_full.parquet) — last 10 of "
                      f"{by_season.height} seasons",
                subtitle="the exact frame the trainers read; regenerated by the model pipeline")
    .fmt_number(columns="plays", sep_mark=",", decimals=0)
    .fmt_number(columns="mean_epa", decimals=4)
)
```

## LOSO evaluation, recomputed from the out-of-fold artifacts

The pipeline persists every model's leave-one-season-out out-of-fold
predictions under `python/artifacts/loso_*_oof.parquet`. Recomputing the
headline metrics from those files — rather than quoting the cards — keeps
this page honest against the artifacts themselves:

```{python}
rows = []
specs = [
    ("EP", "loso_ep_oof.parquet", "ep_pred", "realized", "mae"),
    ("WP (spread)", "loso_wp_oof.parquet", "wp_pred", "y", "brier"),
    ("WP (naive)", "loso_wp_naive_oof.parquet", "wp_pred", "y", "brier"),
    ("FG", "loso_fg_oof.parquet", "fg_pred", "made", "brier"),
    ("QBR", "loso_qbr_oof.parquet", "qbr_pred", "y", "mae"),
    ("xPass", "loso_xpass_oof.parquet", None, None, "brier"),
    ("Two-point", "loso_two_pt_oof.parquet", None, None, "brier"),
    ("Pregame WP", "loso_pgwp_oof.parquet", None, None, "brier"),
]
for name, fname, pred, y, kind in specs:
    p = ART / fname
    if not p.is_file():
        continue
    d = pl.read_parquet(p)
    cols = d.columns
    pred = pred if pred in cols else next((c for c in cols if c.endswith("_pred")), None)
    y = y if (y and y in cols) else next((c for c in cols if c in ("y", "realized", "made", "label")), None)
    if not pred or not y:
        continue
    dd = d.select(pl.col(pred).cast(pl.Float64).alias("p"),
                  pl.col(y).cast(pl.Float64).alias("t")).drop_nulls()
    metric = (float((dd["p"] - dd["t"]).abs().mean()) if kind == "mae"
              else float(((dd["p"] - dd["t"]) ** 2).mean()))
    rows.append({"model": name, "n_oof": dd.height,
                 "metric": "MAE" if kind == "mae" else "Brier", "value": metric})
gt_show(
    GT(pl.DataFrame(rows).to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="LOSO out-of-fold metrics — recomputed at render time",
                subtitle="from python/artifacts/loso_*_oof.parquet; every prediction is from a model that never saw its season")
    .fmt_number(columns="n_oof", sep_mark=",", decimals=0)
    .fmt_number(columns="value", decimals=4)
)
```

## SHAP — the promoted boosters attributed

The five score-time boosters below are the **promoted** artifacts — the
`python/artifacts/v2/` fits, byte-identical to the `.ubj` files sdv-py bundles
in `cfb/models/` (the CP booster is read from that bundle). Their feature
matrices come from the trainer's own analysis export:
`python -m cfb_model_build.model_training export-analysis` writes
`python/artifacts/analysis/analysis_{ep,wp,xpass,cp}.parquet` through the very
`ep_matrix` / `wp_matrix` / `xpass_frame` / `extract_pass_features` code paths
the fits use, so `spread_time`, `adj_TimeSecsRem`, `ExpScoreDiff_Time_Ratio`,
`score_diff` and `era` are the engineered columns the boosters actually saw,
not a re-derivation on this page. TreeSHAP is XGBoost's own
`pred_contribs=True` (no `shap` dependency); the multiclass EP tensor is 3-D
and is averaged over its seven class margins, the binary models are 2-D.

```{python}
#| output: false
import hashlib, json
import importlib.resources as ir
BUNDLE = Path(str(ir.files("sportsdataverse.cfb") / "models"))
AN = ART / "analysis"
MANIFEST = json.loads((AN / "analysis_manifest.json").read_text())

def sha12(p):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(p).read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:12]

def resolve_booster(name):
    """The promoted local copy (python/artifacts/v2/) if present, else the sdv-py bundle."""
    for p in (ART / "v2" / name, BUNDLE / name):
        if p.is_file():
            return p
    raise FileNotFoundError(name)

def load_booster(p):
    b = xgb.Booster(); b.load_model(str(p)); return b

def shap_sample(bst, frame, n=4000, seed=11):
    """(sampled rows, |contribution| (n, p), feature names); the bias column is dropped."""
    feats = bst.feature_names
    s = frame.drop_nulls(subset=feats)
    s = s.sample(n=min(n, s.height), seed=seed)
    X = s.select(feats).to_numpy().astype(np.float32)
    c = bst.predict(xgb.DMatrix(X, feature_names=feats), pred_contribs=True)
    sv = np.abs(c[..., :-1])
    if sv.ndim == 3:          # multi:softprob -> (n, k, p): mean over the k class margins
        sv = sv.mean(axis=1)
    return s, sv, feats

def importance_plot(sv, feats, title):
    sh = pl.DataFrame({"feature": feats, "mean_abs_shap": sv.mean(axis=0).tolist()}).sort("mean_abs_shap", descending=True)
    return (
        ggplot(sh.to_pandas(), aes("reorder(feature, mean_abs_shap)", "mean_abs_shap"))
        + geom_col(fill="#2a6f97") + coord_flip()
        + labs(x="", y="mean |SHAP| (margin space)", title=title)
        + theme_minimal()
    )

SUITE = {  # label -> (artifact, analysis frame, manifest key)
    "EP (7-class)": ("ep_model.ubj", "analysis_ep.parquet", "ep"),
    "WP (spread)": ("wp_spread.ubj", "analysis_wp.parquet", "wp"),
    "WP (naive)": ("wp_naive.ubj", "analysis_wp.parquet", "wp"),
    "xPass": ("xpass_model.ubj", "analysis_xpass.parquet", "xpass"),
    "CP": ("cfb_cp_model.ubj", "analysis_cp.parquet", "cp"),
}
BOOSTERS = {k: load_booster(resolve_booster(a)) for k, (a, _, _) in SUITE.items()}
FRAMES = {f: pl.read_parquet(AN / f) for f in {f for _, f, _ in SUITE.values()}}
SHAP = {k: shap_sample(BOOSTERS[k], FRAMES[f]) for k, (_, f, _) in SUITE.items()}
```

```{python}
from importlib.metadata import PackageNotFoundError, version as _pkg_version
try:
    _sdv_ver = _pkg_version("sportsdataverse")
except PackageNotFoundError:
    _sdv_ver = "unknown"

def _where(p, a):
    return str(p.relative_to(ROOT)).replace("\\", "/") if p.is_relative_to(ART) else f"sdv-py bundle/{a}"

def _trained_on(p):
    """basename of the training frame named in the booster's card (<stem>.json or <stem>.card.json), else None"""
    def find(o):
        if isinstance(o, dict):
            if "training_frame" in o:
                return o["training_frame"]
            for v in o.values():
                r = find(v)
                if r:
                    return r
        return None
    for c in (p.with_suffix(".json"), p.with_suffix(".card.json")):
        if c.is_file():
            tf = find(json.loads(c.read_text()))
            return Path(tf).name if tf else None
    return None

_src = Path(MANIFEST["source_frame"]).name
rows = []
for k, (a, f, m) in SUITE.items():
    p = resolve_booster(a); tf = _trained_on(p)
    rows.append({
        "model": k, "artifact": _where(p, a), "sha256": sha12(p),
        "bundle": "= sdv-py bundle" if (BUNDLE / a).is_file() and sha12(BUNDLE / a) == sha12(p) else "differs",
        "trained_on": tf or "n/a (no card)",
        "frame_ok": "n/a" if tf is None else ("same frame" if tf == _src else "MISMATCH"),
        "n_features": BOOSTERS[k].num_features(),
        "frame_rows": MANIFEST["models"][m]["n_rows"], "sample": SHAP[k][1].shape[0],
    })
prov = pl.DataFrame(rows)
# The narrative below is written for the promoted fits; refuse to render prose about a different booster.
if (prov["bundle"] != "= sdv-py bundle").any() or (prov["frame_ok"] == "MISMATCH").any():
    raise RuntimeError(f"attributed booster is not the promoted one or was trained on a different frame:\n{prov}")
gt_show(
    GT(prov.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Which booster each attribution below explains",
                subtitle=f"analysis frames from {_src} (sha256 {MANIFEST.get('source_sha256', '?')[:12]}, export-analysis "
                         f"{MANIFEST['written'][:10]}); booster sha256 compared against the .ubj bundled in sdv-py "
                         f"{_sdv_ver}; 'trained on' from each booster's card")
    .fmt_number(columns=["frame_rows", "sample"], sep_mark=",", decimals=0)
    .cols_label(model="Model", artifact="Artifact", sha256="sha256[:12]", bundle="vs bundle", trained_on="Trained on",
                frame_ok="Frame", n_features="Features", frame_rows="Frame rows", sample="SHAP sample")
)
```

```{python}
rows = []
for k, (_, sv, feats) in SHAP.items():
    m = sv.mean(axis=0); tot = m.sum()
    for rank, i in enumerate(np.argsort(-m)[:3], start=1):
        rows.append({"model": k, "rank": rank, "feature": feats[i], "mean_abs_shap": float(m[i]),
                     "share": float(m[i] / tot)})
gt_show(
    GT(pl.DataFrame(rows).to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Top-3 features per booster — mean |SHAP| and share of total attribution",
                subtitle="margin space (log-odds; EP: class-margin mean); shares sum to 1 over each model's full feature set")
    .fmt_number(columns="mean_abs_shap", decimals=3)
    .fmt_percent(columns="share", decimals=1)
    .cols_label(model="Model", rank="#", feature="Feature", mean_abs_shap="mean |SHAP|", share="Share")
)
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "WP (spread) mean |SHAP| by season, 1,500 plays per season. A feature whose weight jumps at a rule-era cut (2006/2013/2020) would be doing the era's work; a flat line means the model reads it the same way in every era."
bst = BOOSTERS["WP (spread)"]; feats = bst.feature_names
wpf = FRAMES["analysis_wp.parquet"].drop_nulls(subset=feats)
strat = (wpf.with_columns(pl.int_range(pl.len()).shuffle(seed=11).over("season").alias("_r"))
            .filter(pl.col("_r") < 1500).drop("_r"))
X = strat.select(feats).to_numpy().astype(np.float32)
sv = np.abs(bst.predict(xgb.DMatrix(X, feature_names=feats), pred_contribs=True)[:, :-1])
top6 = [feats[i] for i in np.argsort(-sv.mean(axis=0))[:6]]
by_season = (
    pl.DataFrame({f: sv[:, i] for i, f in enumerate(feats)}).with_columns(season=strat["season"])
    .group_by("season", maintain_order=True).agg([pl.col(f).mean() for f in top6]).sort("season")
    .unpivot(index="season", on=top6, variable_name="feature", value_name="mean_abs_shap")
)
(
    ggplot(by_season.to_pandas(), aes("season", "mean_abs_shap", color="feature"))
    + geom_line() + geom_point(size=1)
    + labs(x="season", y="mean |SHAP| (log-odds)", title="WP (spread): attribution by season, top-6 features")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

What the attributions say — 4,000-play samples (seed 11); the exact values
are in the top-3 table above:

- **EP.** Field position and clock split the top: `yards_to_goal` 34.4% and
  `TimeSecsRem` 33.7% of total attribution, score state
  (`pos_score_diff_start`) third at 16.8%, the four down dummies together
  about 14%. That is the cfbscrapR ordering attributed play-by-play — on the
  promoted booster the first two are effectively tied rather than field
  position clearly first.
- **WP (spread).** Two score-state terms carry it — `ExpScoreDiff_Time_Ratio`
  32.8% and `pos_score_diff_start` 32.1% — with `spread_time` the third
  pillar at 23.4%; no clock or field term exceeds 3%. **WP (naive)** drops
  `spread_time` and that share does not disappear: `pos_score_diff_start`
  absorbs it (32.1% → 48.0%), `ExpScoreDiff_Time_Ratio` holds at 31.2%, and
  `pos_team_receives_2H_kickoff` becomes the third feature (5.5%).
- **xPass** reads the situation first — `down` 31.3%, `distance` 23.7% — then
  score (`pos_score_diff` 16.9%), field position (10.6%) and clock (7.9%);
  `era` and `period` are the tail, so rule-era pass tendency is a small
  effect once down-and-distance is in.
- **CP** is the game-state-only Approach A and attributes like one: `down`
  27.1%, `score_diff` 19.6%, `yards_to_goal` 15.4%, `distance` 9.9%,
  `period` 8.3%. What an air-yards feature would add is the recorded CPOE
  feasibility finding; SHAP cannot supply it here.
- **By season (WP spread, 1,500 plays × 22 seasons).** The score-state terms
  move within a narrow band — `ExpScoreDiff_Time_Ratio` 1.04–1.15,
  `pos_score_diff_start` 0.97–1.17 (extremes at 2016 and 2013),
  `adj_TimeSecsRem` 0.07–0.12 — with no step at the 2006/2013/2020 rule-era
  cuts. `spread_time` is the exception: 0.31 in 2004, about 1.0 from 2013 on
  (0.98 in 2025). That ramp is neither a rule effect nor missing data
  (`spread_time` is non-null in every season): it is the ESPN **default
  spread**. In the training frame every 2004 and 2005 game carries
  `homeTeamSpread = ±2.5` with `gameSpreadAvailable = 0`, as do 57% of 2006
  games, 67% of 2008, 8.7% of 2013 and 5.1% of 2025 — the `cfb_line_odds`
  consensus backfill closed 2,167 games but not the earliest seasons. A
  2.5-point placeholder decays to a near-constant, so the booster has nothing
  to attribute to it, and the early-season WP-spread model runs close to the
  naive one. The fix is upstream of SHAP — a historical-spread source for
  2004–2008 — and belongs with the backfill work, not this page.

## Results — the scored surfaces, identified

```{python}
# pos_team in this frame is the ESPN team id; recover the display name from
# the home/away name columns on any row where the team appears.
mp2 = mp.with_columns(
    pl.when(pl.col("pos_team") == pl.col("homeTeamId"))
    .then(pl.col("homeTeamName")).otherwise(pl.col("awayTeamName")).alias("pos_team_name"))
teams = (
    mp2.filter(pl.col("epa").is_not_null()
               & ((pl.col("pass") == 1) | (pl.col("rush") == 1)))
    .group_by("pos_team")
    .agg(pl.col("pos_team_name").first().alias("offense"),
         pl.len().alias("plays"), pl.col("epa").mean().alias("epa_play"))
    .sort("epa_play", descending=True).head(10)
    .with_columns(
        ("<img src='https://a.espncdn.com/i/teamlogos/ncaa/500/"
         + pl.col("pos_team").cast(pl.Int64).cast(pl.Utf8) + ".png' height='36'/>").alias("logo"))
)
gt_show(
    GT(teams.select("logo", "offense", "plays", "epa_play").to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Top 10 offenses by EPA/play — 2025 model_pbp", subtitle=f"source: {mp_source}")
    .fmt_markdown(columns="logo")
    .fmt_number(columns="plays", sep_mark=",", decimals=0)
    .fmt_number(columns="epa_play", decimals=3)
    .cols_label(logo="", offense="Offense", plays="Plays", epa_play="EPA/play")
)
```

```{python}
# Key on the ESPN athlete id when the frame carries it (stage-10 output from 2026-09-01 on),
# so two passers who share a name never merge; older release frames fall back to the name.
# The frame contract allows a null id on a row that still has a name (~2-3% of named
# passers are regex-fallback names ESPN ships no athlete id for -- see ATHLETE_ID_FLOOR in
# python/cfb_model_build/cfb_model_pbp/build.py). Keying on the id column alone would DROP
# those rows and undercount dropbacks / EPA / CPOE, and can push a passer under the
# 150-dropback cutoff. Coalesce per row instead: id when present, name otherwise.
has_ids = "passer_player_id" in mp2.columns and mp2["passer_player_id"].null_count() < mp2.height
key_expr = (
    pl.coalesce(pl.col("passer_player_id").cast(pl.Int64).cast(pl.Utf8), pl.col("passer_player_name"))
    if has_ids else pl.col("passer_player_name")
).alias("passer_key")
qbs = (
    mp2.filter((pl.col("pass") == 1) & pl.col("epa").is_not_null()
               & pl.col("passer_player_name").is_not_null())
    .with_columns(key_expr, passer=pl.col("passer_player_name"))
    .group_by("passer_key")
    .agg(pl.col("passer").first(), pl.col("pos_team_name").last().alias("team"),
         pl.len().alias("dropbacks"), pl.col("epa").mean().alias("epa_play"),
         pl.col("cpoe").drop_nulls().mean().alias("cpoe"),
         *([pl.col("passer_player_id").drop_nulls().first().alias("passer_player_id")]
           if has_ids else []))
    .filter(pl.col("dropbacks") >= 150)
    .sort("epa_play", descending=True).head(10)
)
cols = ["passer", "team", "dropbacks", "epa_play", "cpoe"]
if has_ids:
    # Headshot only where an athlete id survived the coalesce; a name-keyed row gets "".
    qbs = qbs.with_columns(
        pl.when(pl.col("passer_player_id").is_not_null())
        .then("<img src='https://a.espncdn.com/i/headshots/college-football/players/full/"
              + pl.col("passer_player_id").cast(pl.Int64).cast(pl.Utf8) + ".png' height='40'/>")
        .otherwise(pl.lit("")).alias("headshot"))
    cols = ["headshot"] + cols
sub = (f"source: {mp_source}; keyed by ESPN athlete id (passer_player_id) with a name fallback for "
       "the rows ESPN ships no id for, headshots from a.espncdn.com"
       if has_ids else f"source: {mp_source}; this frame predates the athlete-id columns, so names identify")
g = (
    GT(qbs.select(cols).to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Passer EPA/play leaders with CPOE — 2025 (min 150 dropbacks)", subtitle=sub)
    .fmt_number(columns=["epa_play", "cpoe"], decimals=3)
    .cols_label(passer="Passer", team="Team", dropbacks="Dropbacks", epa_play="EPA/play", cpoe="CPOE")
)
if has_ids:
    g = g.fmt_markdown(columns="headshot").cols_label(headshot="")
gt_show(g)
```

## Provenance & reproducibility

- **Per-model cards** (`ep.md` … `pregame_wp.md`): generated by
  `python -m cfb_model_reports` (stage `cfb_model_70_reports` /
  `scripts/cfb_models.sh 70`) from the training pipeline's artifacts — the
  cards are compiled documents already; regenerating them is part of the
  model pipeline.
- **This page** (`deepdive.qmd` → `deepdive.md`): rendered by
  `scripts/render_model_docs.sh` (Quarto → GFM, `--output-dir .` because
  this directory is also a Quarto website project). Inputs:
  `python/artifacts/` (LOSO OOF parquets, `pbp_full.parquet`, boosters —
  regenerate via `scripts/cfb_models.sh`), the per-model **analysis frames**
  `python/artifacts/analysis/` (`CFB_MODELS_ARGS="export-analysis --pbp
  python/artifacts/pbp_full.parquet --out-dir python/artifacts/analysis"
  scripts/cfb_models.sh 30`, or the same subcommand via
  `python -m cfb_model_build.model_training`; the CI pipeline runs it right
  after `ingest`), the stage-10 scored frame `python/artifacts/model_pbp_2025.parquet`
  when present (`scripts/cfb_models.sh 10` for the season), and the published
  `espn_cfb_model_pbp` / `cfb_ratings` releases (cached under
  `docs/models/.cache/`, gitignored).
- **Training data:** seasons 2004–2025 (the corpus table above is computed
  from the exact training frame). Models, gates and lineage:
  `models/manifest.yaml`, `models/REGISTRY.md`.
- **Forward-looking notes** live in [roadmap.md](roadmap.md) — the
  hand-authored companion the generator cannot clobber.

## Avenues for improvement & open issues

- **Resolved (2026-09-01, PR #56):** *Per-model SHAP for the full suite* —
  the trainer now exports the engineered feature matrix per model
  (`export-analysis` → `python/artifacts/analysis/analysis_{ep,wp,xpass,cp}.parquet`,
  built through the same `*_matrix` code paths the fits use) and this page
  attributes EP, WP-spread, WP-naive, xPass and CP against the promoted
  boosters, with a by-season slice for WP.
- **Resolved (2026-09-01, PR #56):** *Athlete ids in model_pbp* — the ids
  were never absent upstream (sdv-py's participants module emits them and
  every final.json carried them); the model_pbp builder's `DESCRIPTOR_COLS`
  was the drop point. The frame now carries `passer_player_id`,
  `rusher_player_name`/`_id`, `receiver_player_name`/`_id` (Int64, additive),
  and the passer table keys on the id and ships headshots. The published
  release gains the columns on its next stage-10 + publish run.
- **Known issue:** `python/artifacts/` is a build tree, not committed — a
  fresh clone must run the model pipeline before this page renders. That is
  deliberate (artifacts are large), but it makes this page's reproducibility
  contingent on the pipeline run; the cards' generator has the same property.
